plan.vision: A strict Spec Roadmap detailing the exact Agentic problem, atomic milestones, and Testing Strategy. The project aims to manage and optimize coding sessions for developers, ensuring they can enter a flow state more easily and manage their time effectively. Atomic milestones include: 1. Defining session management logic, 2. Implementing session tracking and optimization, 3. Creating a user-friendly interface, 4. Developing a comprehensive test suite. The testing strategy will involve unit tests for core logic, integration tests for session management, and end-to-end tests for the entire application.

session_tracker.py: def track_session_activity(session_id: str, activity: str) -> None
session_optimizer.py: def optimize_session(session_id: str, optimization_params: dict) -> dict

plan.lessons_learned: This project avoids past mistakes by using memory-mapped files for efficient data handling, prioritizing algorithmic efficiency over OOP overhead, and ensuring that all dependencies are pinned in a virtual environment. The repository will be kept lightweight by excluding heavy directories with .gitignore, and clear setup scripts will be provided for reproducibility. Additionally, the project will focus on security and isolation, ensuring that the code executed within the sandbox cannot access or modify external resources. There are no hidden paid-API dependencies.
plan.commit_message: Implement a session manager for optimizing and managing coding sessions.

files_to_generate.instructions: Contains the core logic for starting, stopping, and getting the status of a coding session. Use pure functions and dependency injection to ensure testability.
Handles the tracking of activities during a coding session. This includes logging and retrieving session activities. Ensure all I/O operations are decoupled from the core logic.
Provides functionality to optimize a coding session based on given parameters. The optimization should be done in a way that is agnostic to specific session configurations.

Implements the user interface for the session manager. This includes functions for displaying session status and collecting session configuration from the user. Keep the UI simple and focused on the core functionality.

Contains the unit tests for the session manager, session tracker, and session optimizer. Import and use the actual generated modules. Do NOT create mock or stub classes for the core logic. The code MUST pass its own tests.
Include entries to ignore venv, __pycache__, and .env files. Ensure the repository remains lightweight and free of unnecessary files.
Provide a detailed explanation of the architecture, how to set up the project, and how to run the tests. Include a section on the design decisions and how they align with the GSD framework.
